 Election Day is here: everything you need to know 
 NBC6 will provide special coverage across all platforms throughout the day, with the latest voting updates and election results. 
 By NBC6 • 
 Published 2 hours ago • 
 Updated on November 2, 2026 at 4:08 pm 
 BOOKMARKER

 What to Know
 Rules for voting in person. Read here . 
 What time do polls open and close in Florida? Here's the schedule. 
 Candidates for governor, Senate and key races 
 Election Day is here, and Florida voters are heading to the polls to cast their ballots in some of the state’s most important races and decide key issues, as well as local contests.
 Watch NBC6 free wherever you are
   WATCH HERE 
 Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
 NBC6 will provide special coverage across all platforms throughout the day, with the latest voting updates and election results.
What do I need to vote in Florida?
Before heading to the polls, make sure you're ready to vote.
 Be registered to vote. 
Register to vote or update your information
 Bring a valid photo ID. 
Florida voters must present a current, valid photo ID with a signature. If the photo ID does not include a signature, an additional ID with the voter's signature is required. See the accepted forms of ID below.
 Know where to vote. 
Find your polling place
 Choose how to vote. 
Florida voters can vote early, by mail or on Election Day.
Explore your voting options
Accepted forms of voter ID
For the November 3, 2026, general election, Florida voters must present a current, valid photo ID with a signature. If the photo ID does not include a signature, an additional ID with the voter's signature is required.
 • Florida driver's license
 • Florida identification card issued by the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles
 • U.S. passport
 • Debit or credit card
 • Military identification
 • Student identification
 • Retirement center identification
 • Neighborhood association identification
 • Public assistance identification
 • Veteran health identification card issued by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
 • Concealed weapon or firearm license issued under Florida Statute 790.06
 • Federal, state, county or municipal government employee identification
 Important: If your photo ID does not include a signature, you must present another form of identification that includes your signature. If you do not have the required identification, you may vote using a provisional ballot. A voter information card is not an accepted form of identification for voting.
 Looking ahead to 2027: Florida approved changes to its voter identification requirements under HB 991 (Chapter 2026-26). The new requirements take effect January 1, 2027, after the November 2026 general election.
 Official sources: 
Florida Statute 101.043 — Identification required at polls
Florida HB 991 (2026) — Effective date: January 1, 2027

 This year, Floridians will find three amendments to the Florida Constitution on the ballot. Below, you can review what they are.
Three constitutional amendments on Florida's ballot
Amendment 1
Budget stabilization fund
Would increase the state's Budget Stabilization Fund limit from 10% to 25% of general revenue collections. It would also require annual transfers of up to $750 million , unless certain conditions are met, and allow withdrawals for critical state needs.
View official text
Amendment 2
Agricultural property tax exemption
Would exempt certain tangible personal property located on agricultural land and used for agricultural production or agritourism activities from property taxes. The property must belong to the agricultural landowner or leaseholder. The exemption would first apply to tax years beginning Jan. 1, 2027 .
View official text
Amendment 3
Property taxes
Would increase the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 , with inflation adjustments thereafter. It would also reduce the annual assessment increase cap for non-homestead properties from 10% to 5% . Certain new Florida residents would have to wait until their fifth year of qualifying for the homestead exemption to receive the increase, subject to federal constitutional limits. The measure would also establish new rules for the use of property tax revenue.
View official text
 Important: Each amendment requires at least 60% of the votes cast on the measure to pass.
